html:
SMTO-GML-0066 — SMTO needs an .eml email file to import

GUID: 9770113b-729e-46fa-80c3-03de002b2162
Slug: gmail-eml-import-invalid
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gmail-client-actions

What happened

  • Importing into Gmail works only with a saved email file whose name ends in .eml and that contains a real email. The file given was empty, a different type, or didn't look like an email, so nothing was imported.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Export or save the email from your mail program as a file whose name ends in .eml. Gmail imports whole saved emails, and .eml is the standard file type for them.
  2. Make sure the file isn't empty, opens as an email in a mail program, and is smaller than 25 MB. Empty, damaged or oversized files are refused before anything is sent to Gmail.
  3. Attach the file with Add files to conversation in the composer, then ask SMTO to import that file. SMTO can only import a file it can open from this conversation.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the email as imported, and it appears in your Gmail.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste the email's raw contents into the conversation instead; attach the file.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gmail import_message rejected the source: the file reference does not have a .eml filename, or its content is empty or has no parseable message headers.

What this means

  • Import resolves an authorized artifact or upload before provider mutation, requires an .eml filename and parsed message headers, and retains the normal 25 MiB file limit.

Why this can happen

  • Import resolves an authorized artifact or upload before provider mutation, requires an .eml filename and parsed message headers, and retains the normal 25 MiB file limit.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the selected account, action arguments and operation reference; do not infer mailbox effects from the error alone.

How to fix it

  • Provide an authorized artifact or upload whose filename ends in .eml and whose bytes parse with message headers (email.parser.BytesHeaderParser), within the 25 MiB file limit. The check in gmail/client_actions.execute_action runs before the effect is reserved or anything is sent to Gmail.
  • Choose an accessible .eml export or upload and submit its file reference.

Retry and execution caution

  • Choose an accessible .eml export or upload and submit its file reference.

How to verify the fix

  • The artifact passes validation before the import is sent.

What not to do

  • Do not paste binary mail content into model context or automatically replay an uncertain import.

Technical notes

  • This check rejects new work before its write. It does not undo previous confirmed effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
